# Studienstiftung Summary
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany’s largest scholarship provider for exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates, offering both financial and academic support since its founding in Dresden in 1925. Dissolved under National Socialism in 1934 and re-established in Cologne in 1948, the foundation functions independently of political or religious affiliation and does not require German or EU citizenship, nor enforce age limits. Admission is highly selective and occurs through nomination by schools, professors, examination boards, competition achievement, alumni, or by applicant assessment tests, with further entry paths for artists and musicians. In 2023, 13,626 undergraduate/graduate and 1,262 doctoral scholars were supported, constituting around 0.48% of German university students.
Studienstiftung scholarships offer a monthly expense allowance (€300), need-based support up to €855 per month for students, and €1,550 (rising to €1,650 in October 2025) plus a research grant for PhDs, with additional funds for scholars with children. Academic support includes summer schools, research groups, workshops, mentoring, and seminar participation, with scholars regularly reporting on their activities and progress. There are also internal and open cooperative programs (e.g., KAUST, McCloy, ERP, Carlo-Schmid, and the Max Weber program in Bavaria). Notable alumni include numerous Nobel and Leibniz Prize winners, leading academics, business leaders, politicians, artists, and journalists, illustrating its wide impact on German society and international research.
